CONNECTIVITY IN US-EAST-1
=============================

Two VPCs are deployed in us-east-1:

1. vpc-ff1b8158 contains 3 instances with shared network connectivity:

   - LaunchTemplateInstance (i-e6fe8b05355d4c35d)
   - WebServerInstance (i-c51f8f1c195a7d680)

2. vpc-default contains 1 instance isolated in its own VPC:
   - MyEC2Instance (i-ec7bba6f31771cb9e)

The three instances in vpc-ff1b8158 can communicate with each other through the VPC's internal routing.
The instance in vpc-default operates in a separate network namespace and cannot directly communicate
with instances in vpc-ff1b8158 without an explicit peering connection or transit gateway.

commands: # Get all EC2 instances across the three regions with their security groups # and launch template info regions=("us-east-1" "us-west-1" "us-west-2") # Collect all instances across regions echo "Gathering instance data..." >&2 for region in "${regions[@]}"; do aws ec2 describe-instances \ --region "$region" \ --output json | jq -r '.Reservations[] | .Instances[] | { Region: "'$region'", InstanceId, InstanceType, State: .State.Name, PublicIpAddress, SecurityGroups: [.SecurityGroups[].GroupId], LaunchTemplate: .LaunchTemplate }' > "/tmp/${region}-instances.json" done # Combine all instances jq -s 'add' /tmp/us-east-1-instances.json /tmp/us-west-1-instances.json /tmp/us-west-2-instances.json 2>/dev/null || echo "[]"

# Better approach - get all instances with key info regions=("us-east-1" "us-west-1" "us-west-2") all_instances="[]" for region in "${regions[@]}"; do instances=$(aws ec2 describe-instances \ --region "$region" \ --output json | jq -r '.Reservations[] | .Instances[] | { Region: "'$region'", InstanceId, InstanceType, State: .State.Name, PublicIpAddress, PrivateIpAddress, SecurityGroupIds: [.SecurityGroups[].GroupId], LaunchTemplate: .LaunchTemplate }') # Append to our collection if [ -z "$all_instances" ] || [ "$all_instances" = "[]" ]; then all_instances="$instances" else all_instances=$(echo -e "$all_instances\n$instances") fi done # Output all instances found echo "$all_instances" | jq -s '.'

# Get all unique security group IDs from instances regions=("us-east-1" "us-west-1" "us-west-2") # Collect all unique security group IDs declare -A sg_set for region in "${regions[@]}"; do aws ec2 describe-instances \ --region "$region" \ --output json | jq -r '.Reservations[] | .Instances[] | .SecurityGroups[].GroupId' | while read sg; do sg_set["$sg:$region"]=1 done done # Now get security group details for each region for region in "${regions[@]}"; do echo "=== Security Groups in $region ===" >&2 aws ec2 describe-security-groups \ --region "$region" \ --output json | jq -r '.SecurityGroups[] | { Region: "'$region'", GroupId, GroupName, IngressRules: [.IpPermissions[] | select(.IpProtocol == "tcp" or .IpProtocol == "-1") | { FromPort, ToPort, IpProtocol, IpRanges: [.IpRanges[].CidrIp], Ipv6Ranges: [.Ipv6Ranges[].CidrIpv6] }] }' > "/tmp/sgs-${region}.json" done # Combine and filter for relevant security groups cat /tmp/sgs-*.json | jq -s 'add'

# Better approach - get all SGs with full details regions=("us-east-1" "us-west-1" "us-west-2") for region in "${regions[@]}"; do aws ec2 describe-security-groups \ --region "$region" \ --output json | jq '.SecurityGroups[] | { Region: "'$region'", GroupId, GroupName, VpcId, IpPermissions }' done

# Now let's correlate: which instances use which security groups, # and which security groups allow SSH from 0.0.0.0/0 echo "=== Security Groups allowing SSH from 0.0.0.0/0 ===" >&2 # Find all SGs allowing SSH from 0.0.0.0/0 regions=("us-east-1" "us-west-1" "us-west-2") ssh_accessible_sgs=() for region in "${regions[@]}"; do aws ec2 describe-security-groups \ --region "$region" \ --output json | jq -r '.SecurityGroups[] | select(.IpPermissions[] | select(.FromPort == 22 or .FromPort == null) and (.ToPort == 22 or .ToPort == null or .FromPort == null) and (.IpRanges[]?.CidrIp == "0.0.0.0/0") ) | {Region: "'$region'", GroupId, GroupName}' | while read -r line; do if [ ! -z "$line" ]; then echo "$line" fi done done | jq -s '.' echo "" echo "=== Instances with public IPs and SSH-accessible security groups ===" >&2 # Now find instances that use these SGs and have public IPs regions=("us-east-1" "us-west-1" "us-west-2") for region in "${regions[@]}"; do aws ec2 describe-instances \ --region "$region" \ --query 'Reservations[].Instances[?PublicIpAddress != null]' \ --output json | jq -r '.[] | select(.SecurityGroups[].GroupId == "sg-3a309e3934df4eb93" or .SecurityGroups[].GroupId | contains("webSecurityGroup")) | { Region: "'$region'", InstanceId, InstanceType, State: .State.Name, PublicIpAddress, SecurityGroupIds: [.SecurityGroups[].GroupId], SecurityGroupNames: [.SecurityGroups[].GroupName] }' done | jq -s '.'

# Simpler approach - find instances with sg-3a309e3934df4eb93 regions=("us-east-1" "us-west-1" "us-west-2") echo "Instances using SSH-accessible security groups:" >&2 echo "" for region in "${regions[@]}"; do aws ec2 describe-instances \ --region "$region" \ --output json | jq '.Reservations[].Instances[] | select(.SecurityGroups[]?.GroupId == "sg-3a309e3934df4eb93" and .PublicIpAddress != null) | { Region: "'$region'", InstanceId, InstanceType, State: .State.Name, PublicIpAddress, PrivateIpAddress, SecurityGroupIds: [.SecurityGroups[].GroupId], SecurityGroupNames: [.SecurityGroups[].GroupName] }' done | jq -s '.'
